accepted.s: The Faraizi Movement, founded in East Bengal, primarily aimed at:
o: Enforcing the religious duties known as faraiz and purging un-Islamic practices
accepted.x: The Faraizi Movement sought to enforce religious duties, or faraiz, and remove un-Islamic practices. It was founded by Haji Shariatullah in East Bengal.
accepted.tq: Identify the movement from its distinctive objective and religious terminology.
accepted.sec: Faraizi Movement - founder, later leader, region

accepted.s: Who founded the Faraizi Movement in East Bengal in 1818?
accepted.x: Haji Shariatullah founded the Faraizi Movement in East Bengal in 1818. Dudu Miyan, his son, later led the movement.
accepted.tq: Separate the founder from the later leader while retaining the date.
accepted.sec: Faraizi Movement - founder, later leader, region

accepted.s: Dudu Miyan transformed the Faraizi Movement into a movement primarily directed against:
o: British missionary institutions and Parsi reformers
accepted.x: Dudu Miyan, the son of Haji Shariatullah, converted the Faraizi Movement into a peasant movement against zamindars and indigo planters.
accepted.tq: Apply the movement’s social base and immediate opponents to a rural conflict.
accepted.sec: Faraizi Movement - founder, later leader, region

accepted.s: Which sequence correctly represents the institutional development of the Aligarh educational initiative?
o: College classes in 1877 — school in 1875 — AMU in 1920
School in 1875 — college classes in 1877 — AMU in 1920
AMU in 1920 — school in 1875 — college classes in 1877
School in 1877 — college classes in 1920 — AMU in 1875
accepted.x: The Aligarh institution began as a school in 1875, college classes started in 1877, and it became Aligarh Muslim University in 1920.
accepted.tq: Arrange the institutional stages by first identifying the earliest year.
accepted.sec: Aligarh Movement - initial objective, MAO College year and principals, later leaders, AMU conversion

accepted.s: The educational model of the Muhammadan Anglo-Oriental College at Aligarh was based on:
o: Khalsa College and Singh Sabha schools
Traditional madrasas of Patna and Deoband
accepted.x: The Muhammadan Anglo-Oriental College was modelled on Oxford and Cambridge. It was intended to provide modern education to Muslims.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the institutional model from the movement’s broader political orientation.
accepted.sec: Aligarh Movement - initial objective, MAO College year and principals, later leaders, AMU conversion

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the Aligarh Movement:
1. It emerged against the background of the educational backwardness of Muslims after 1857.
2. It encouraged a rational reading of Islam.
3. It was associated with cooperation with the British.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The movement sought Muslim social and educational uplift through modern education, rational religious interpretation and cooperation with the British.
accepted.tq: Check each statement against the movement’s background, intellectual approach and political attitude.
accepted.sec: Aligarh Movement - initial objective, MAO College year and principals, later leaders, AMU conversion

accepted.s: Which of the following was NOT associated with the later leadership of the Aligarh Movement?
accepted.x: Baba Dayal Das was associated with the Nirankari movement. Chiragh Ali, Altaf Husain Hali and Mohsin-ul-Mulk were later leaders associated with the Aligarh Movement.
accepted.tq: Find the person belonging to a neighbouring reform movement rather than the named movement.
accepted.sec: Aligarh Movement - initial objective, MAO College year and principals, later leaders, AMU conversion

accepted.s: Who served as a British principal of the Muhammadan Anglo-Oriental College in addition to Theodore Beck?
accepted.x: Theodore Morison was another British principal of the Muhammadan Anglo-Oriental College. The other three were later Muslim leaders associated with the Aligarh Movement.
accepted.tq: Separate British institutional administrators from later Indian movement leaders.
accepted.sec: Aligarh Movement - initial objective, MAO College year and principals, later leaders, AMU conversion

accepted.s: The Wahabi Movement in India was named after:
accepted.x: The movement was named after Abdul Wahab of Arabia, although its Indian founder was Syed Ahmad Barelvi.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the ideological namesake from the Indian founder.
accepted.sec: Wahabi Movement - Indian founder, chief centre, trials, Andhra leader, anti-British stance

accepted.s:
Arrange the following events connected with the Wahabi Movement in chronological order:
A. Ambala trial
B. Arrest of Mubariz-ud-Daula
C. Patna trial
D. Suppression of the movement
accepted.x: Mubariz-ud-Daula was arrested in 1839, followed by the Ambala trial in 1864, the Patna trial in 1865 and suppression of the movement by 1870.
accepted.tq: Use the dated events as anchors and place the undated suppression after the trials.
accepted.sec: Wahabi Movement - Indian founder, chief centre, trials, Andhra leader, anti-British stance

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the Wahabi Movement is correct?
o: It was suppressed by 1857 after remaining confined to Bengal.
It supported British influence in the Deccan and rejected armed resistance.
It was primarily a Parsi educational movement centred in Bombay.
It fought the Sikhs in Punjab and subsequently opposed the British.
accepted.x: The movement first fought the Sikhs in Punjab and then fought the British. It was suppressed by 1870 and was anti-British in character.
accepted.tq: Test the movement’s changing military target and overall political character.
accepted.sec: Wahabi Movement - Indian founder, chief centre, trials, Andhra leader, anti-British stance

accepted.s: Mubariz-ud-Daula, associated with Wahabi activity in Hyderabad, was:
o: A Parsi reformer who edited Rast Goftar
A brother of the Nizam who resisted British influence in the Deccan
A principal of the Aligarh college
A Sikh mahant who controlled gurdwaras in Punjab
accepted.x: Mubariz-ud-Daula was the Nizam’s brother. Influenced by Syed Ahmad Barelvi, he attempted to organise resistance to British influence in the Deccan and died in prison after his arrest.
accepted.tq: Match the regional leader with his family position and political activity.
accepted.sec: Wahabi Movement - Indian founder, chief centre, trials, Andhra leader, anti-British stance

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: The Indian Musalmans — Sayyid Ahmad Khan
accepted.x: W.W. Hunter wrote The Indian Musalmans in 1871. Sayyid Ahmad Khan wrote Asbab-e-Baghawat-e-Hind, while Rast Goftar was associated with Parsi reform.
accepted.tq: Start with the sure book–author pair and eliminate cross-movement substitutions.
accepted.sec: Book → author on Muslims under British rule

accepted.s: Asbab-e-Baghawat-e-Hind was written by:
accepted.x: Asbab-e-Baghawat-e-Hind was written by Sayyid Ahmad Khan. W.W. Hunter authored The Indian Musalmans.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between two books dealing with Muslims under British rule.
accepted.sec: Book → author on Muslims under British rule

accepted.s: The Ahmadiya Movement was founded by Mirza Ghulam Ahmad at Qadian in:
accepted.x: Mirza Ghulam Ahmad founded the Ahmadiya Movement at Qadian in Punjab in 1889.
accepted.tq: Use the place–founder–year combination to distinguish the movement from Aligarh and Sikh reform movements.
accepted.sec: Ahmadiya Movement - founder, place, beliefs

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT a belief or feature associated with the Ahmadiya Movement?
o: A liberal and universal conception of religion
Unqualified acceptance of orthodox Muslim objections to its founder’s claims
Promotion of Western liberal education among Muslims
accepted.x: The Ahmadiya Movement promoted liberal and universal religious ideas, opposed jihad and supported Western liberal education. Orthodox Muslims rejected Mirza Ghulam Ahmad’s claim to be a messiah.
accepted.tq: Identify the statement that reverses the movement’s relationship with orthodox criticism.
accepted.sec: Ahmadiya Movement - founder, place, beliefs

accepted.s: Qadian, associated with the foundation of the Ahmadiya Movement, is located in:
accepted.x: Qadian is in Gurdaspur district of Punjab. It was the place where Mirza Ghulam Ahmad founded the Ahmadiya Movement.
accepted.tq: Use the precise location rather than the broader regional label alone.
accepted.sec: Ahmadiya Movement - founder, place, beliefs

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Movement)
a. Nirankari
b. Namdhari or Kuka
c. Singh Sabha
d. Akali

List-II (Leader or feature)
i. Removal of corrupt mahants from gurdwaras
ii. Baba Dayal Das and belief in Nirankar
iii. Baba Ram Singh and Bhaini
a. Gurmukhi and Punjabi literature
accepted.x: Nirankari was associated with Baba Dayal Das and the formless God; Namdhari with Baba Ram Singh and Bhaini; Singh Sabha with Gurmukhi and Punjabi literature; and Akali with removal of corrupt mahants.
accepted.tq: Start from the distinctive Nirankar and mahant associations to secure the code.
accepted.sec: Sikh reform - Kuka, Singh Sabha, Akali movement, Gurdwara Act

accepted.s: The Singh Sabha movement was associated with which of the following developments?
o: Opposition to all forms of Sikh education
Promotion of Gurmukhi and Punjabi literature
Establishment of the Faraizi peasant movement
accepted.x: The Singh Sabha movement promoted Gurmukhi and Punjabi literature. It was associated with Singh Sabha centres at Amritsar and Lahore and with Khalsa College, Amritsar.
accepted.tq: Link the reform organisation with its specific literary and educational programme.
accepted.sec: Sikh reform - Kuka, Singh Sabha, Akali movement, Gurdwara Act

accepted.s: Which of the following chronology is correct regarding institutions associated with the Singh Sabha movement?
o: Khalsa College, Amritsar — 1873; Singh Sabha at Amritsar — 1879; Singh Sabha at Lahore — 1892
Singh Sabha at Amritsar — 1873; Singh Sabha at Lahore — 1879; Khalsa College, Amritsar — 1892
Singh Sabha at Lahore — 1873; Khalsa College, Amritsar — 1879; Singh Sabha at Amritsar — 1892
Singh Sabha at Amritsar — 1892; Singh Sabha at Lahore — 1879; Khalsa College, Amritsar — 1873
accepted.x: The Singh Sabha was established at Amritsar in 1873 and Lahore in 1879. Khalsa College at Amritsar was established in 1892.
accepted.tq: Arrange the three dated Sikh reform developments from earliest to latest.
accepted.sec: Sikh reform - Kuka, Singh Sabha, Akali movement, Gurdwara Act

accepted.s: Which statement best describes the significance of Ram Singh Kuka in the Sikh reform tradition?
o: He was the first to use non-cooperation and boycott of British goods.
He founded the Ahmadiya Movement at Qadian.
He introduced Urdu as the language of Osmania University.
He founded the Rahnumai Mazdayasnan Sabha in Bombay.
accepted.x: Ram Singh Kuka is noted as the first to use non-cooperation and boycott of British goods. He was later exiled to Rangoon after the 1872 Malerkotla clash.
accepted.tq: Identify the distinctive method associated with the correct Sikh leader.
accepted.sec: Sikh reform - Kuka, Singh Sabha, Akali movement, Gurdwara Act

accepted.s: The Sikh Gurdwaras Act of 1925 placed gurdwaras under the control of the:
accepted.x: The Sikh Gurdwaras Act, 1925 placed gurdwaras under the Shiromani Gurdwara Parbandhak Committee, or SGPC. This represented a major success of the Akali Movement.
accepted.tq: Match the legislation with the institutional authority created or recognised by it.
accepted.sec: Sikh reform - Kuka, Singh Sabha, Akali movement, Gurdwara Act

accepted.s: Which of the following was NOT a focus of the Rahnumai Mazdayasnan Sabha?
accepted.x: The Sabha focused on girls’ education, reform of marriage customs and opposition to orthodoxy. Gurdwara management belonged to the Sikh reform context, particularly the Akali movement.
accepted.tq: Find the item belonging to a different religious reform tradition.
accepted.sec: Parsi reform - Rahnumai Mazdayasnan Sabha, founders, Rast Goftar

accepted.s: Rast Goftar, the organ of the Parsi reform movement, means:
accepted.x: Rast Goftar means “Truth-teller.” It was the organ of the Rahnumai Mazdayasnan Sabha and was edited by Dadabhai Naoroji.
accepted.tq: Use the exact meaning of the named journal rather than a broad reform slogan.
accepted.sec: Parsi reform - Rahnumai Mazdayasnan Sabha, founders, Rast Goftar

accepted.s: Who edited Rast Goftar, the organ associated with the Rahnumai Mazdayasnan Sabha?
accepted.x: Dadabhai Naoroji edited Rast Goftar. He was also one of the founders of the Rahnumai Mazdayasnan Sabha.
accepted.tq: Separate the journal editor from the other founders listed with him.
accepted.sec: Parsi reform - Rahnumai Mazdayasnan Sabha, founders, Rast Goftar

accepted.s: Nasaraiah, who was popular among the Madigas, preached:
o: The superiority of zamindars over peasants
The necessity of armed jihad against all Western education
One God and opposition to idol worship
The establishment of Sikh gurdwara committees
accepted.x: Nasaraiah, a Sayyid Muslim who died in 1825, preached belief in one God and opposed idol worship. He was associated with the Vinukonda–Narasaraopet region of Guntur.
accepted.tq: Connect the regional reformer with his central religious teaching.
accepted.sec: Muslim reform in Hyderabad and Andhra

accepted.s: Nasaraiah was associated with which region of present-day Andhra Pradesh?
accepted.x: Nasaraiah was associated with the Vinukonda–Narasaraopet area of Guntur. He was popular among the Madigas and preached monotheism.
accepted.tq: Use the precise Andhra regional association to distinguish similar reformers.
accepted.sec: Muslim reform in Hyderabad and Andhra

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements about Osmania University is correct?
o: It was established at Bombay in 1851 and taught through Gujarati.
It was established at Qadian in 1889 and taught through Punjabi.
It was established at Aligarh in 1920 and taught only through Persian.
It was established at Hyderabad in 1918 and taught through Urdu.
accepted.x: Osmania University was established at Hyderabad in 1918 and taught in Urdu. It conferred an honorary D.Litt. on B.R. Ambedkar in 1953.
accepted.tq: Combine the institution’s place, year and medium of instruction.
accepted.sec: Muslim reform in Hyderabad and Andhra

accepted.s: Osmania University conferred an honorary D.Litt. on B.R. Ambedkar in:
accepted.x: Osmania University, established in Hyderabad in 1918, conferred an honorary D.Litt. on B.R. Ambedkar in 1953.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the university’s founding year from the later honorary degree year.
accepted.sec: Muslim reform in Hyderabad and Andhra

accepted.s: Which comparison between the Aligarh and Deoband movements is correctly stated?
o: Aligarh emphasised Western education and cooperation with the British, whereas Deoband represented an orthodox and anti-British strand.
Aligarh was orthodox and anti-British, whereas Deoband promoted Western education and cooperation with the British.
Both movements rejected modern education and supported British colonial rule.
Both movements were primarily Sikh and Parsi reform organisations.
accepted.x: Aligarh promoted Western education and was broadly pro-British and anti-Congress, whereas Deoband preserved an orthodox, anti-British and pro-Congress strand.
accepted.tq: Test the reversed-comparison trap by separating educational orientation from political stance.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: Which of the following statements correctly expresses the broader significance of the Aligarh and Deoband movements?
o: Deoband created the modern educated Muslim middle class, while Aligarh opposed all modern education.
Aligarh helped build a modern educated Muslim middle class, while Deoband kept alive an orthodox and anti-colonial strand.
Aligarh and Deoband were both exclusively movements for Sikh gurdwara reform.
Neither movement had an educational or political significance.
accepted.x: Aligarh contributed to the growth of a modern educated Muslim middle class. Deoband preserved an orthodox and anti-colonial tendency within Muslim public life.
accepted.tq: Match each movement with its distinctive historical contribution rather than reversing them.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: Sayyid Ahmad Khan’s later political conservatism has been criticised for:
o: Sowing the seeds of communal division
accepted.x: A criticism of Sayyid Ahmad Khan’s later political conservatism is that it sowed the seeds of communal division. This criticism is distinct from the educational objectives of the Aligarh Movement.
accepted.tq: Identify the stated historical criticism without confusing it with institutional achievements.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: Which statement reflects the criticism concerning the political position of the Deoband movement?
o: It was founded to promote Parsi marriage reform.
It supported British rule because it rejected all anti-colonial activity.
It supported Congress largely to oppose Sir Syed rather than from a positive political creed.
It sought to replace Gurmukhi with Urdu in Sikh institutions.
accepted.x: One criticism holds that Deoband supported Congress more as a means of opposing Sir Syed than from an independently developed positive political creed.
accepted.tq: Distinguish a historiographical criticism from the movement’s general political description.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: Which of the following legal pairings is correctly matched?
accepted.x: Parsi marriages are governed by the Parsi Marriage and Divorce Act, 1936. The Sikh Anand Marriage Act dates to 1909 and was amended in 2012 to allow registration.
accepted.tq: Separate the original enactment year from the later amendment year and the other community’s law.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: The Sikh Anand Marriage Act, 1909 was amended in 2012 to:
o: Abolish the practice of idol worship among Madigas
Introduce Urdu as the medium of higher education
accepted.x: The Sikh Anand Marriage Act, 1909 was amended in 2012 to allow registration of Sikh marriages. Gurdwara administration was dealt with by the Sikh Gurdwaras Act, 1925.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the purpose of the marriage-law amendment from the separate gurdwara legislation.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: Which movement is identified among the earliest movements to resist British rule in Punjab?
accepted.x: The Namdharis are identified among the earliest movements that resisted British rule in Punjab. The other options belonged to different regional or religious reform contexts.
accepted.tq: Use the regional resistance clue to distinguish the Namdhari movement from reform associations elsewhere.
accepted.sec: Universal angles
